brief: A seed-starting tray of at least four cells, each with a draining bin.

requirements.requirement: Seed-starting tray of at least four cells
requirements.evidence: Four hex base pieces at (0,0), (-1,0), (0,-1), (1,0) on level 0, all touching the centre cell; capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied; check_build ok with meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a draining bin
requirements.evidence: Each of the four cells holds a 'Bin, full depth, drained' (hex-bin-full-drain) tray; each was filled with soil and planted with a seedling-stage plug plant (props 1-4).

requirements.requirement: Draining function works physically (water drains out)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only; drainage holes are modelled but water flow and material performance cannot be verified here.

finish.summary: Built a four-cell seed-starting tray: four hex bases in a flower cluster, each holding a full-depth drained bin, capped on open faces and joint-locked. Each bin has soil and a seedling plug plant. check_build is clean with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
